(a) The Secretary, after consultation with the Secretary of Energy, shall establish uniform standards for data collection which shall be used by States in all reports required under this title. 
    (b)
        (1) The standards established by the Secretary under this section shall apply to (A) information concerning home energy consumption, (B) the cost and type of fuels used, (C) the type of fuel used by various income groups, (D) the number and income levels of households assisted by this title, and (E) any other information which the Secretary determines to be reasonably necessary to carry out the provisions of this title. 
        (2) In carrying out this section, the Secretary shall analyze information supplied by the Secretary of Energy on the price structure of various types of fuel, particularly the increases in such price structure as it relates to the financial assistance provided under this title.  
    (c) The Secretary shall report annually to Congress concerning data collected under subsection (b).

fable.w: The tempting reading is that "consultation" and the reference to States signal participation, but the only consultation is between two federal cabinet secretaries, which is intra-government coordination. States merely use the standards in their reports and are not consulted in setting them. The annual report goes to Congress, which is also inside the federal government. The section says "establish uniform standards" without expressly requiring a regulation or public comment, so it is not clearly rulemaking either.
fable.s: The Secretary, after consultation with the Secretary of Energy, shall establish uniform standards for data collection which shall be used by States in all reports required under this title.

qwen_block.w: The consultation described is between two federal officials (the Secretary and the Secretary of Energy), which constitutes intra-governmental coordination, not participation by outside parties. The requirement for States to use these standards for reporting is a regulatory compliance obligation, not a mechanism for States to participate in the decision-making process itself. The annual report to Congress is also an internal government communication.
qwen_block.s: (a) The Secretary, after consultation with the Secretary of Energy, shall establish uniform standards for data collection which shall be used by States in all reports required under this title.

opus.w: The only consultation here is between two federal officials, the Secretary and the Secretary of Energy, so it never crosses the federal boundary. The States only use the standards to report data; they are not consulted before the decision. The annual report goes to Congress, which is inside the federal government. The standards are not described as being set by regulation, so there is no rulemaking or comment period, though that is the one point on which a reader could reasonably disagree.
opus.s: The Secretary, after consultation with the Secretary of Energy, shall establish uniform standards for data collection which shall be used by States in all reports required under this title.
opus.b: The tempting reading is "Yes," because the Secretary must act "after consultation" before setting standards, and setting standards can look like rulemaking. That reading fails: the consultation is only with the Secretary of Energy, another federal official. The section also never says the standards are set by regulation. The States only use the standards and submit reports. The annual report goes to Congress, which is also inside the federal government.

qwen_chat.w: The consultation mentioned is between the Secretary (of HHS, implied by context of energy assistance) and the Secretary of Energy. Both are federal officials, so this is intra-governmental coordination, not participation by outside parties. The requirement for States to submit reports is a compliance obligation, not a participatory process in the decision-making. The report to Congress is also internal to the government.
qwen_chat.s: (a) The Secretary, after consultation with the Secretary of Energy, shall establish uniform standards for data collection which shall be used by States in all reports required under this title.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "consultation with the Secretary of Energy" constitutes participation because it involves coordination before a decision (establishing standards). However, the Secretary of Energy is a federal official, and coordination between federal agencies is explicitly excluded from the definition of participation. The other interactions involve States submitting reports (which is not participation in the decision-making process, but rather compliance with reporting requirements) and the Secretary reporting to Congress (which is internal to the government).
